subject: Ocean sunfish
topic: This giant swimming head was spotted by a NOAA robot in deep water off Florida.
script:
This giant swimming head was spotted by a NOAA robot in deep water off Florida.
It's an ocean sunfish, the largest bony fish in the world.
It can weigh up to a thousand kilograms.
It looks like a fish that's all head, with two tall fins sticking out.
Its name comes from its habit of lying flat at the surface, warming up in the sun.
But sunfish also dive deep, hundreds of meters down, to hunt jellyfish and other prey.
Basking at the surface may help them warm back up after a cold dive.
Seeing one this deep, from a robot's camera, is a rare treat.
Would you want to meet one up close?
